about: CS-1239 display-rounding goldens. Every expected string is derived by hand from the stated rule: scale |value| by 10^places, split into whole + remainder, round the remainder by ROUND_HALF_EVEN (a tie goes to the even whole), render the whole with places digits after the point, and drop the sign of a result that rounds to zero. half_up is the hand-derived answer under ROUND_HALF_UP (a tie goes away from zero); it differs from expected exactly when flips is true.

cases.name: half_at_0
cases.why: 0.5 is a tie between 0 and 1; 0 is even. Half-up goes away from zero to 1.

cases.name: three_halves_at_0
cases.why: 1.5 is a tie between 1 and 2; 2 is even, and 2 is also away from zero, so both modes agree.

cases.name: five_halves_at_0
cases.why: 2.5 is a tie between 2 and 3; 2 is even. Half-up gives 3.

cases.name: seven_halves_at_0
cases.why: 3.5 is a tie between 3 and 4; 4 is even and away from zero.

cases.name: minus_five_halves_at_0
cases.why: -2.5: magnitude 2.5 ties to the even 2, sign restored. Half-up goes away from zero to -3.

cases.name: minus_three_halves_at_0
cases.why: -1.5: magnitude ties to the even 2; away from zero is also 2.

cases.name: minus_half_at_0
cases.why: -0.5: magnitude ties to the even 0, and a zero result carries no sign. Half-up gives -1.

cases.name: eighth_at_2
cases.why: 0.125 scaled by 100 is 12.5, a tie between 12 and 13; 12 is even.

cases.name: three_eighths_at_2
cases.why: 0.375 scaled is 37.5, a tie between 37 and 38; 38 is even and away from zero.

cases.name: five_eighths_at_2
cases.why: 0.625 scaled is 62.5, a tie; 62 is even.

cases.name: minus_eighth_at_2
cases.why: -0.125: magnitude 12.5 ties to the even 12, sign restored because 12 is not zero.

cases.name: sixteenth_at_3
cases.why: 0.0625 scaled by 1000 is 62.5, a tie; 62 is even. The leading zero after the point is kept.

cases.name: twentieth_at_1
cases.why: 0.05 scaled by 10 is 0.5, a tie between 0 and 1; 0 is even.

cases.name: minus_twentieth_at_1
cases.why: -0.05 ties to the even 0, and a zero result carries no sign, so not -0.0.

cases.name: tie_that_carries_at_2
cases.why: 4.995 scaled is 499.5, a tie between 499 and 500; 500 is even, and the carry ripples into the units.

cases.name: tie_that_carries_at_0
cases.why: 9.5 ties between 9 and 10; 10 is even and gains a digit.

cases.name: ten_thirds_at_2
cases.why: 3.3333... scaled is 333.33..., remainder 1/3 is below a half, so 333.

cases.name: two_thirds_at_2
cases.why: 66.66... has remainder 2/3, above a half, so 67.

cases.name: minus_two_thirds_at_2
cases.why: Magnitude rounds to 67 as above, sign restored.

cases.name: third_at_0
cases.why: Remainder 1/3 is below a half.

cases.name: just_above_a_tie_at_2
cases.why: 1/8 + 10^-30. Scaled it is 12.5 + 10^-28, strictly above the tie, so 13 in both modes. A route through a 28-digit decimal context would first round the value to 0.125 exactly and then tie it DOWN to 0.12 - the double rounding this case exists to catch.

cases.name: tiny_negative_at_2
cases.why: -0.001 scaled is -0.1; magnitude remainder 1/10 is below a half, result zero, so no sign.

cases.name: zero_at_2
cases.why: Zero, padded to two places.

cases.name: whole_at_0
cases.why: An integer-valued Fraction at no places renders with no point.

cases.name: whole_at_2
cases.why: Padded with two zeros.

cases.name: half_at_3
cases.why: 0.5 is exact at three places; nothing to round, zeros padded.
